payload.title: The learning lens's mechanisms tuple is a hand copy of memory.LEARNING_EVENT_KINDS, pinned in the test by a second hand-typed set, so a kind added to the closed vocabulary appears in rows_by_kind but is never scored or evaluated for quarantine
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/autonomy_evidence.py:1478-1484 (the five mechanisms typed in the lens spec)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/memory.py:27 (LEARNING_EVENT_KINDS, the closed vocabulary F1.1 landed)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/autonomy_evidence.py:4702-4705 (the scorecard scores only the listed mechanisms)
aria-kernel/tests/test_scorecard_lens_specs.py:49-50 (_JOURNAL_KINDS, a third typed copy, not memory.LEARNING_EVENT_KINDS)
payload.rule_violated: One owner per concept (CLAUDE.md single-center rule): the closed learning-event vocabulary has one owner in memory.py; the scorecard must read it, not restate it.
payload.notes: A sixth kind is added to LEARNING_EVENT_KINDS (and its writer). memory.py accepts it, but the scorecard never lists it in mechanisms, so its contribution is not computed and it can never be a quarantine candidate; the test still passes because it compares the lens to its own typed set. Close condition: Build the lens's mechanisms from memory.LEARNING_EVENT_KINDS (or assert equality in a test) and replace the test's typed set with the owner's tuple; a test that adds a kind to the owner's tuple and expects it in mechanism_scorecard()['mechanisms']. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
